newsitem.title: UK: UK grain futures close lower on currency, tender.
newsitem.headline: UK grain futures close lower on currency, tender.

text.p: A strong pound sterling against other European currencies and the European Union (EU) weekly grain tender depressed UK grain futures on Thursday.
The EU granted licences for 256,500 tonnes of free market wheat at 15.97 Ecus maximum rebate and 279,125 tonnes of barley at 31.49 Ecus maximum rebate.
Traders said the result was within market expectation and had already been factored into prices.

"If the EU had granted 300,000 to 350,000 tonnes of wheat after what was said in Brussels on Wednesday, then some people would have taken it as bullish news, but this was about what we expected," said a trader.
On Wednesday EU Commission Director-General David Roberts said the EU would have to pursue a cautious grain export subsidy policy for the rest of 1996/97 (July-June) due to budgetary problems.
Lower French wheat prices also weigh on the UK market.
At the close wheat futures were two to 2.10 stg down on a turnover of 792 lots while barley was one stg down after trading 62 lots.
Amsterdam milling wheat futures were again unchanged and tradeless.
